subject: Clarify SOC 2 period endpoints and point-in-time evidence
messages:
From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@finova.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@auditors.co>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 report period — endpoint semantics and point-in-time items

Hi Dylan,

We're preparing the SOC 2 review checklist for our underwriting team and had a couple of precise questions about Redwood's Type II report period so our auditors can map controls correctly. Two quick things:

1) Period endpoints — is the end date reported in your Type II report inclusive or exclusive? For example, if the report states coverage from 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30, should we treat activity on 2024-06-30 (23:59:59 UTC) as in-scope or out-of-scope?

2) Point-in-time evidence — some controls cite "periodic point-in-time snapshots" (e.g., configuration baselines, IAM access listings). Do you provide specific point-in-time artifacts (timestamped exports) tied to the report period, or are point checks performed at other dates and documented as exceptions?

Our external auditor (cc'd) needs these clarified before finalizing our SIG questionnaire. A short confirmation, ideally with any standard phrasing you prefer us to use in the SIG/SOC mapping, would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martin
Information Security Manager
Finova Inc.

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@finova.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@auditors.co>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report period — endpoint semantics and point-in-time items

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Marissa (compliance) and Neha (security ops) to confirm exact wording we use for auditors.

A couple of quick notes from my side so the auditor has context:
- Our standard Type II covers an inclusive start date and an inclusive end date (we treat the listed end date as inclusive of activity through 23:59:59 UTC on that date).
- For point-in-time evidence, we maintain timestamped exports for a subset of controls (configuration baselines, access listings, KMS key rotation records). We commonly provide these as supporting artifacts on request — sometimes as a separate "point-in-time attachments" bundle.

Marissa / Neha — could you confirm the formal phrasing and whether you can supply the bridge-letter template + a sample point-in-time artifact listing for Finova's auditor?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive — Compliance & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, Alex Martin <alex.martin@finova.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Priya Singh <priya.singh@auditors.co>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report period — endpoint semantics and point-in-time items

Hi all — confirming the formal positions below; copying the language we typically provide auditors.

1) Period endpoints (formal): "The SOC 2 Type II examination report issued by [Firm] for Redwood Inference covers the inclusive period from 2023-07-01 through 2024-06-30 (all times referenced as UTC). Activities occurring on the end date (2024-06-30) up to 23:59:59 UTC are considered in-scope for the examination period."

2) Point-in-time evidence (formal): "Where controls require point-in-time evidence, Redwood produces timestamped exports or snapshots (for example, configuration baselines, IAM role/access listings, and key rotation logs) from production systems. These artifacts are correlated to the SOC 2 period on request; where continuous monitoring exists, we will provide the nearest available export or sampled artifact along with the timestamp and extraction method."

We can provide:
- The PDF of the SOC 2 Type II report (attached as a stub here).
- A bridge-letter draft that states the exam covered the inclusive dates and explains our point-in-time artifacts (attached).
- A short index (CSV) listing the point-in-time artifacts available and their timestamps — note some artifacts are generated weekly or nightly, so the exact timestamp may be the closest snapshot within the period.

Priya — please confirm if that phrasing is sufficient or if you need more granular logs (e.g., per-request audit events versus daily exports).

Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2023-07-01_to_2024-06-30.pdf (report stub), Bridge_Letter_Draft_Redwood.docx (draft)

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@auditors.co>

Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report period — endpoint semantics and point-in-time items

Thanks, Marissa — that wording is clear and should work for our mapping. A couple of follow-ups:

- Confirmation of timezone: we'll record UTC in our evidence index. Good to know you use UTC for reporting.
- Point-in-time granularity: daily/nightly exports are acceptable for controls that require a configuration baseline or user-role listing. For controls tied to cryptographic key rotation we may request the rotation entry for the exact rotation event if it falls on the period boundary.
- Bridge letter: the draft looks fine; we ask that Redwood sign and date the bridge letter on company letterhead and include the contact for any follow-up evidence requests.

Alex — if you can confirm the desired date for Redwood to return the signed bridge letter and the index of available artifacts, we'll schedule the review.

Regards,
Priya Singh
Senior Auditor
Auditors & Co.
